newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Lippo group's medical unit to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Lippo group's medical unit to float shares.

text.p: Indonesian medical services firm PT Siloam Gleaneagles Health Care, a unit of the Lippo Group, said on Thursday that it will float 47 million shares on the Surabaya Stock Exchange on March 26.
The company said it would offer shares at a price of 2,950 rupiah each during a three-day offering period starting March 10.
Lippo Securities is the lead underwriter, the company said.

Siloam said of the proceeds of about 138.7 billion rupiah, 28.7 percent or about 39.8 billion rupiah would be used to buy a stake in PT Nusa Medika Utama, which would build a 250-bed hospital in the Lippo Cikarang industrial and housing estate in Bekasi on the eastern outskirts of Jakarta.

The company said 20.3 percent, or about 28.1 billion rupiah, would be allocated for the purchase of a stake in PT Budi Mulia Gleaneagles Hospital and also for renovation of the Surabaya-based Budi Mulia hospital.
Siloam said 13.6 percent of the proceeds would be used to buy a stake in PT Sentralindo Wirasta, which is to build a 200-bed capacity hospital in East Jakarta.

Another 13.6 percent would be used to enlarge its stake in PT Eramulia Pratamajaya, which would build a 200-bed capacity hospital in South Jakarta, and another 13.6 percent would be used to develop three medical clinics in Jakarta.
The company said the remaining 10.2 percent would be used to increase its stake in PT Aritasindo Permaisemesta which would establish a 200-bed capacity in Bandung, West Java.
